header: Date: 2025-03-04 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 47m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Alex Duarte (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Borealis), Lena Ortiz (Borealis), Tom Greenwood (Borealis), Priya Rao (Borealis)
summary: Introductory hosted API demo focusing on embeddings + reranker endpoints, demo of Redwood Console Optimize suggestions for batching and caching, security discussion (SOC2, SSO, KMS questions), and agreement to run a short pilot; action items and pricing follow-up agreed.
topics: Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO, KMS, data retention
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on accounts for search and relevance. Alex is our SE and he'll run through the demo and some numbers. Samir: thanks, Maya. Were excited to see the hosted flow.
[00:20] Alex Duarte: Great, hi all. Quick agenda: embeddings endpoint, reranker endpoint, Console Optimize suggestions, and then Q&A and pilot scope.
[00:35] Samir Patel: Quick context — Borealis is powering product search for 12m monthly users, current infra is Elastic + custom ranker, latency target sub 120ms for frontend, budgets tight, also need audit logs and SSO.
[00:55] Lena Ortiz: we have a labeled set of ~50k queries, relevance labels 0-3, and want to improve top-3 precision. We also batch updates nightly.
[01:10] Alex Duarte: Perfect, that maps well. We'll show hosted embeddings for vector store, then the rerank endpoint which accepts candidate docs + query embeddings or tokens and returns re-ranked list with scores. A note: in hosted mode, we provide prefix/K V cache management and auto-batching; the Console gives profiling per-route.
[01:35] Tom Greenwood: Can you talk about data retention? We need logs for 90 days, but can't have raw query text stored beyond 30 days without opt-in.
[01:50] Maya Chen: Yep. Hosted API has retention settings per account; by default we retain logs 30 days but offer enterprise retention add-ons. For PII we recommend token-level redaction; we also support customer-managed KMS for encrypted at rest keys in Private deployments.
[02:10] Priya Rao: SOC2? Do you have an ISO cert?
[02:15] Maya Chen: SOC2 Type II is available — I'll send the pack. ISO is in progress. We'll add links in the follow-up.
[02:25] Samir Patel: Good. On pricing, are embeddings invoiced per vector and rerank per token like generation?
[02:35] Alex Duarte: Embeddings are per vector unit. Reranker is billed per request + per-token for the re-ranking model if you use a generative ranker; but we also provide a lightweight ML rank scorer option which is cheaper — we can show tradeoffs later.
[02:55] [00:03:00] Alex Duarte: Ok demo time. Im switching to the hosted Console. (screen descriptions: Console: models catalog, routes, Optimize hints) The embeddings endpoint is /v1/embeddings, we show batch call examples and the telemetry panel that shows latency breakdown and per-token cost.
[03:25] Alex Duarte: Note: the Console's Optimize tab suggests batch size 32 for this workload, prefix cache enabled, and a quantization profile if you choose to pin a smaller model. The recommend comes from our Optimize engine which looks at sequence length histograms and cost targets.
[03:50] Lena Ortiz: How does the rerank endpoint accept candidates? We currently return top-200 from ES and want Redwood to rerank top-20.
[04:05] Alex Duarte: Two options: server-side rerank where you send candidate doc ids plus embeddings and we fetch vectors from your vectorstore via connector, or pass the candidate text/payload directly in the request body. For performance, sending embeddings is fastest because we avoid re-embedding.
[04:25] Samir Patel: If we send embeddings for 200 candidates, that's a lot of vector bytes — cost spike?
[04:35] Alex Duarte: True, that's why often teams send top-50 or top-100 and then let the Redwood reranker fine-tune top-20; Optimize suggests a cutover point based on throughput SLOs. Our routing can fall back to a lighter model on spikes.
[04:55] [00:04:55] Maya Chen: On the note of spikes, Redwood has smart routing — you can route by latency SLO or by cost tier. If the primary rerank model is busy, requests go to a cheaper variant or to a cached prefix result.
[05:15] Tom Greenwood: Do you support VPC peering for hosted?
[05:22] Maya Chen: Hosted supports private endpoints and dedicated capacity; for full VPC peering we recommend Redwood Private. But for dedicated pool customers we can set up private endpoints and tighter networking.
[05:40] Lena Ortiz: Can the Console show per-query explanations or feature attributions for reranks?
[05:50] Alex Duarte: We can surface model scores, token-level contributions in some cases, and the Console will show per-route trace for a request including latency bubbles and token breakdown. Attribution isn't perfect — sometimes we label features heuristically.
[06:10] [00:06:10] Samir Patel: We care about latency — will reranking add 80-200ms to our stack?
[06:18] Alex Duarte: Typical hosted rerank with a compact ranker is 20-60ms additional on our infra for a top-20 set. Generative rankers are more variable, with median ~80-150ms depending on sequence length. That is why Optimize suggests caching and smaller sequence windows to hit sub-100ms.
[06:40] Maya Chen: In our dedicated customers we've seen more consistent tails — that's the tradeoff between hosted cost-efficiency and dedicated predictability.
[06:55] [00:06:55] Lena Ortiz: What's the best way to evaluate improvements? Do you have an eval harness?
[07:05] Alex Duarte: Yes, we have an eval harness and script. You provide query/label CSV and we'll run precision@k, MRR and A/B with your baseline. We'll also run a small held-out live A/B if you want.
[07:25] Priya Rao: Any PII redaction tooling? We might need to hash or remove IDs before sending.
[07:32] Maya Chen: We recommend client-side redaction; we have a small SDK utility to scrub common patterns, and we support customer-managed KMS if you're doing encryption at rest.
[07:45] [00:07:45] Alex Duarte: Now I'll show a live rerank demo. Ill call the hosted embeddings endpoint for a sample query and then call rerank with candidates. (audio: typing) Heres request payload: query: "wireless headphones noise canceling"; candidates: 50 snippets from a product feed.
[08:15] Alex Duarte: Results: baseline ES score top-3 had items A, C, D. Redwood rerank pushed item B to top-1 because semantic match and negative phrase match penalized item A. Note: the Console shows the score delta and an option to lock in the reranker as the final.
[08:40] Lena Ortiz: The example is nice. Does the reranker return confidence or explanation?
[08:48] Alex Duarte: It returns a score and optional explain tokens. If you enable explain it adds ~10-20ms.
[08:55] [00:08:55] Samir Patel: Can we host our own rerank model on your runtime (bring-your-own-model)?
[09:05] Alex Duarte: Yes — BYOM is supported in Dedicated and Private. In hosted we can host custom components as managed model deployments under certain enterprise contracts; otherwise use our curated model catalog.
[09:20] Tom Greenwood: For the pilot we prefer hosted to avoid infra setup. What would the pilot look like?
[09:30] Maya Chen: Typical pilot: 2 weeks, Redwood ingests your sample data, runs offline evals, sets up a 1% live A/B traffic for two days, then we compare metrics. We'll scope exact volume and SLOs in the kickoff.
[09:45] [00:09:45] Alex Duarte: Operational note: batching impacts latency vs cost. Optimize will suggest a batching window and max batch size. For interactive search we tune small batches and rely on prefix/K V cache to reduce tokens. For high throughput we increase batch size.
[10:10] Lena Ortiz: Does the Console surface cost by route and token?
[10:16] Maya Chen: Yes, token-level cost breakdown is visible; Console also highlights hot routes and suggests quantization or cheaper model variants.
[10:30] Samir Patel: About security: SAML SSO for our team, audit logs per request, RBAC for routes — do you support those?
[10:40] Maya Chen: Yes to SAML/SSO and audit logs. RBAC is available to set role permissions per route. We also support HSM/KMS integrations for Private customers.
[10:55] [00:10:55] Alex Duarte: A small gotcha — embeddings dimensionality mismatch can happen if you re-embed with a different model. Optimize will warn if vectors look incompatible. We recommend standardizing on a single embeddings model for indexing and retrieval, or mapping between vector spaces if needed.
[11:20] Tom Greenwood: How do we instrument tracing? We already use OpenTelemetry.
[11:26] Alex Duarte: We have tracing hooks and can export traces to your collector. Console will also ingest traces for correlation if you give an ingest token.
[11:40] [00:11:40] Maya Chen: Quick commercial note: hosted pilot usually covered by Redwood credits; production pricing will be per vector + rerank and can include a minimum commit for Reserved/Dedicated if you pick that. I'll share a pricing sheet.
[11:58] Priya Rao: In case of outage how do fallbacks work? We need graceful degradation.
[12:05] Alex Duarte: You can configure fallback policies per route — e.g., return baseline ES ranking if Redwood rerank fails, or call a cached fallback response. We also support region failover.
[12:25] [00:12:25] Samir Patel: Ok last technical Q: quantization recommendations — do you automate that?
[12:33] Alex Duarte: Optimize suggests quant profiles based on your sequence length and acceptable quality delta. We don't force quantization; we show expected token-cost savings and an estimated hit on accuracy.
[12:50] Lena Ortiz: How do we compare different rerank models? Is there an eval UI?
12:55 Alex Duarte: Yes — Eval UI in Console allows you to lift baselines, run against labels, visualize PR curves and set up regression alerts. We'll include sample screenshots.
[13:10] [00:13:10] Maya Chen: All right, if it's useful I'll recap next steps now.
[13:15] Samir Patel: Please do.
[13:18] Maya Chen: Recap: 1) Redwood will run a short baseline rerank bench with your sample logs (Alex owns) 2) Well share SOC2/security pack and pricing (Maya owns) 3) Customer to upload anonymized logs and labels (Samir/Lena) 4) Schedule Poc kickoff — target week of 3/11. Any objections?
[13:40] Samir Patel: Sounds good. One more ask — can you include estimated total cost for a 1% live A/B at current traffic?
[13:48] Maya Chen: We can provide a cost estimate in the pricing follow-up.
[13:54] [00:13:54] Priya Rao: Thanks, that's helpful.
[14:00] Maya Chen: Great. Well send notes and links. Thanks everyone, well follow up with actionable items.
[14:10] Alex Duarte: Thanks all.
[14:12] Samir Patel: Thanks.
[14:15] End of call.
